narrative.overview:
Every page stands on one of Edward's own photographs, full bleed and fixed behind everything: the canal at golden hour, Kyoto bamboo, New York at night. Over that ground floats real liquid glass: a translucent, warm-tinted material with live backdrop blur and saturation, a specular sheen, a light rim brighter at the top left, and, on Chromium, true edge refraction from SVG displacement maps. Glass carries the controls and the short, urgent things (nav, hero, buttons, chips, the atom bubble, dialogs). When reading gets dense, warm sand-paper sheets slide up over the photo with large rounded top corners, and the page alternates between looking through the glass at the photograph and reading on paper.

The world is calm, human and tactile. Its palette is sampled from the canal photo, not picked from a UI kit: dark mossy forest ink, sand paper, and gold from sunlight on water. Type pairs a high-contrast editorial serif (Instrument Serif, always weight 400) for names, headings and numerals with a warm grotesk (Hanken Grotesk) for everything that has to work. Motion is a soft spring: glass squashes when pressed, sections rise out of a blur, the cursor is a drop of glass that bends the photograph under it.

It explicitly refuses the category default for developer portfolios (dark neon with glow and mono labels) and its opposite (a white Swiss card grid), and it replaces the site's former violet, cyan and pink palette with a more human one.
keyCharacteristics: Owner photography as the ground on every page, fixed behind content, with a soft radial vignette.
One glass material in four tints: clear, panel, reading, smoke; opal when it sits on paper.
Paper sheets (34px top corners, 34px overlap) for dense reading, alternating with windows onto the photo.
Instrument Serif at weight 400 only; Hanken Grotesk for body and UI; no uppercase tracking labels.
Every control is a pill; spring easing `cubic-bezier(.32, .72, 0, 1)` throughout.
Product pages keep the world and swap a single accent.

rules.name: The Sampled Palette Rule
rules.body: Every hue comes from the ground photography's warm golds and mossy darks. No saturated blues, violets, cyans or pinks; the one cool tone in the build is the chrono-app's sky grey.

rules.name: The Readable Gold Rule
rules.body: Sun gold (sun) appears only on dark surfaces or over the photo. On paper, gold text is always sun-ink (5.46:1 on paper), and inside reading glass it is sun-ink-reading.

rules.name: The One Accent Per Product Rule
rules.body: A product page changes `--accent` and `--accent-soft` and nothing else. Layout, glass, type and neutrals stay identical across Memive, Chrono and Scadoo.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks, Sans Works Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif is used only at weight 400, for names, headings, numerals and italic accents. Hierarchy in serif comes from size and italics, never from bolding it. Hanken Grotesk carries body, buttons, navigation and labels.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Headings stand on their own: no uppercase, tracked eyebrow labels above them. The build has no `text-transform: uppercase` anywhere in the shared system.

rules.name: The Lens Not Card Rule
rules.body: Glass is always translucent, with blur, saturation, rim light and a cast shadow. A glass surface is never an opaque fill with a drop shadow.

rules.name: The Reading Glass Rule
rules.body: Any glass panel that carries paragraphs over the photo (hero, about, contact, product heroes, panels) switches to the reading tint (`glass-reading`) with a white-to-honey veil (`linear-gradient(160deg, rgba(255,253,247,.55), rgba(255,250,236,.1) 50%, rgba(238,222,184,.32))`), and darkens its secondary ink and gold to `ink-2-reading` and `sun-ink-reading`, so text stays legible where dark forest sits behind it.

rules.name: The Opal On Paper Rule
rules.body: Glass on paper has nothing to refract, so it becomes opal: a white `.55` tint, a crisp white top edge, a forest hairline, no refraction filter. A dark button on paper becomes solid forest.

dos: Do stand every page on an owner photograph in the fixed ground layer, with its radial vignette, and choose its focal point with `--focus`.
Do use the glass material for controls and short content over the photo, and switch to the reading tint as soon as a panel carries paragraphs.
Do move dense reading onto paper sheets that overlap the window by `34px`.
Do keep one smoke-glass primary button per action group, with the trailing arrow icon in its circular well.
Do use sun-ink (or the product accent) for gold and accent text on paper, and sun only on dark or over the photo.
Do show only real app screenshots, in the glass phone frame, each with a provenance sidecar beside the raster.
Do drive motion with the spring curve and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: Don't build a dark neon developer portfolio with glows and mono labels, or a white Swiss card grid; both are the defaults this world refuses.
Don't bring back the violet, cyan and pink palette, or any saturated hue the photography does not contain.
Don't bold Instrument Serif, or set uppercase tracked eyebrows above headings.
Don't put sun gold text or cream text on paper.
Don't apply clear glass or refraction on paper; it has nothing to bend there and becomes opal.
Don't use emoji or icon fonts; icons are inline SVG line drawings in `currentColor`.
Don't use monospace outside real code.
